title: Var vs Let Hoisting Analyzer
problemStatement: Implement `analyzeHoisting(varCodeStr)` that inspects a simple code snippet and determines whether accessing a variable before its declaration returns `undefined` (hoisted with var) or throws a `ReferenceError` (hoisted into TDZ with let/const). Return 'INITIALIZED_UNDEFINED' or 'TDZ_REFERENCE_ERROR'.
interviewTrap: Believing that `let` and `const` are not hoisted at all. They ARE hoisted to the top of the block, but stay uninitialized in the TDZ.

testCases.name: var declaration is initialized to undefined

details.name: var declaration is initialized to undefined

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: In JavaScript execution contexts, variable declarations are processed during the Creation Phase. `var` is hoisted and initialized to `undefined`. In contrast, `let` and `const` are hoisted into the Lexical Environment but remain *uninitialized*. The span of code from block entry until the actual declaration is evaluated is the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ).
stepByStepWalkthrough: Analyze code or variable access simulation.
For `var`, access before declaration yields `undefined` without error.
For `let` or `const`, access before declaration throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access variable before initialization`.
Our analyzer parses/evaluates variable lifecycle states: 'hoisted-initialized' for var vs 'tdz-uninitialized' for let/const.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In V8, Environment Records contain bindings with an initialization state flag. When `var` binding is instantiated, V8 assigns the special internal `the_hole` value and immediately overwrites it with `undefined`. For `let`/`const`, the binding is left pointing to `the_hole`. Any bytecode instruction (e.g. `LdaCurrentContextSlot`) encountering `the_hole` triggers a runtime ReferenceError.

complexity.time: O(1) constant time classification of declaration types.

edgeCasesHandled: var declarations inside blocks do not have block scope; they hoist to the function/global boundary.
let/const inside blocks create a new block lexical environment record with its own TDZ.
typeof operator on a TDZ variable throws a ReferenceError (unlike undeclared variables which return 'undefined').

specifications: ECMA-262 §14.3.1 Let and Const Declarations (Static Semantics and TDZ specification)
ECMA-262 §9.1.1.1.6 GetBindingValue (Throws ReferenceError if binding is uninitialized)
MDN Web Docs: Temporal Dead Zone
verifiedRules: Accessing let/const prior to lexical declaration must throw ReferenceError.
Variables declared with var are initialized to undefined upon environment instantiation.
